title: Session-to-session messaging: termal_send_to_session MCP tool (peer root sessions, queue-if-busy)
outcome:
Let an agent in one root-level session deliver a message/prompt to ANOTHER root-level (peer) session.
Distinct from delegations (which are parent->child): no delegation record, peer-to-peer.

FEASIBILITY: the delivery + queue-if-busy already exist. dispatch_turn (src/turn_dispatch.rs:642) queues
on the target's pending-prompt FIFO when it is Active/Approval, dispatches when idle. POST
/api/sessions/{id}/messages -> send_message -> dispatch_turn_and_snapshot already does this for any
session (Telegram forwarding uses the same path). So no 'fail if busy' needed — queue is free.

INITIAL SCOPE (this task): fire-and-forget MCP tool.
 - termal_send_to_session({ sessionId, message }) in src/delegation_mcp.rs — thin wrapper that POSTs
   { text: message } to /api/sessions/{sessionId}/messages and returns a compact { sessionId, delivered }.
   Queue-if-busy handled automatically by the backend. Does NOT wait for/return the target's response.
 - Update delegation_mcp_tools_list_exposes_parent_scoped_tools_only expected vector (learned this the
   hard way on tm-px5).

DEFERRED / open design:
 - Discovery: the agent needs the target session id. Defer a termal_list_sessions tool; for now the id
   is supplied by the user/orchestrator.
 - Scope guard: currently can target ANY session id (incl. a delegation child or self). Consider limiting
   to root (non-child) sessions in the same project.
 - Request/response: fire-and-forget only for now; a wait/result path (like delegations) is a later add.
disposal_reason: Backlog triage w-930e4d333f07 (Architect1 batch 3b, spot-checked by Termal::Fable2): CLOSE-DONE. termal_send_to_session exists and is in daily use (commits 0a1e144, fa13d81); its "blocked" state came only from a migrated dependency.
